headline: High: shared filesystem and broad shell/write privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem, and Agent A explicitly shares state with other instances via filesystem while Agent B uses a project directory plus plan-local sandbox. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's files as trusted input. No clipboard or browser bridge is shown, so this is not higher.
conditions: IF Agent B reads files written by Agent A as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace, attacker-controlled file content can cross between them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable auto-ingest of peer-written files.
Require provenance labels on shared artifacts.
Review any file-based prompts before execution.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches files in cwd and has broad network egress; Agent B also reads and writes the project directory and can send data to Plandex Cloud or a self-hosted server. Shared filesystem access means sensitive source code or files in cwd can flow from one agent to the other and then out over network paths. The profiles do not show PHI or regulated data, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them.
IF either agent forwards workspace contents to its backend or configured model provider, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate per-agent directories.
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks.
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately after a test run.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state, while Agent A shares state via filesystem and Agent B shares state via Plandex server backend. Concurrent edits to the same repo or directory can race and corrupt git state or overwrite files. Because these defaults are dangerous and no locking is documented, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository, write conflicts can occur.
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is active, state corruption becomes likely.
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time.
Use separate branches per agent.
Add a manual merge checkpoint.
Disable auto-apply on one agent.
Snapshot the repo before parallel work.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can emit tool-driven code or file changes, and Agent B has review-then-apply with optional auto-apply mode, so A's output can become B's authoritative input. Without a documented verification barrier between them, mistakes or fabricated details from A can cascade into B's applied changes. The pair's defaults make this a high-risk workflow.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A's outputs without independent verification, errors propagate.
IF Agent B is in auto-apply mode, downstream actions can be committed automatically.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Force B out of auto-apply mode.
Add a validation step before apply.
Limit A to draft-only outputs.
Compare outputs against source files before merging.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only compliance-relevant signals are generic cloud/model-provider calls and local file access, which do not by themselves prove a breach. Because no specific regulated-data pathway is shown, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace and sent to a noncompliant backend, a compliance issue arises.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the configured backend, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Confirm backend residency settings.
Review retention defaults before use.
Use self-hosted endpoints where required.
